title.narrative: Ethiopian Asylum Seekers Humanitarian Response Project

description.narrative:
Following the political instability in Ethiopia in the month of February 2018, civilians crossed over to Kenya in great numbers seeking asylum and triggering a humanitarian crisis. This was occasioned by the alleged government shooting that left nine civilians dead and scores injured. The influx of the Ethiopian asylum seekers in Kenya prompted action by the Kenya Government (both National and County), host communities and humanitarian organizations to provide basic needs and services e.g. security, shelter, food and water to the affected population. This led to the establishment of two temporary camps by the Kenyan government initially hosting 9,700 people. The established camps are Somare and Dambala Fachana located in Somare and Dambala Fachana locations respectively. Somare camp is adjacent to the Kenyan Ethiopia Border while Dambala Fachana is seventeen kilometers away from the same border.
The political situation in Ethiopia improved after the inauguration of the new Prime Minister on April 2, 2018. This by the willingness of some asylum seekers who went back to their country reducing the number of asylum seekers to approximately 5000 persons. CSG meeting attended by Diocese of Marsbait and CAFOD agreed on 5,000 figure.
The host community has limited resources for example water yet they are magnanimous in their hospitality to the asylum seekers and continues to bear the brunt of sharing scant resources with the Ethiopian asylum seekers.
The management and coordination of the Ethiopian Asylum Seekers’ activities are going on well through the Sub-County Steering Committee (SCSC) chaired by the Moyale Sub-County Commissioner.
